chunks.content: 96 It’s not the price. It’s that you’re ignoring the seller’s ask. The #1 Reason Your LOIs Keep Getting Rejected Hi Sara, Let’s talk about the last “A” in my M.A.F.I.A. framework: Asking Price. No, this isn’t just the number on the listing. This is about understanding what the seller actually wants—and if you skip this step, your offer might go straight in the trash. I see this mistake constantly. A buyer does all the right things—market research, adjusted EBITDA, checks financing, studies industry multiples—and then they drop a number without ever asking... “What does the seller actually care about?” Here are some things to consider: Is the seller trying to lease you the building they own? Do they want to make sure their team stays employed? Are they emotionally attached to their client base? These things matter a lot. And if your LOI doesn’t speak to them, you’ll lose to someone whose offer is lower but smarter. Here’s how to fix it: Use the seller’s language in your LOI. Reference things they mentioned in emails or calls. Show them you listened—and that your offer reflects their goals, not just your spreadsheet. It’s not about caving to every demand. It’s about being strategic with your positioning and human in your approach. Sellers want to feel like their legacy isn’t going to be bulldozed. So next time you draft that LOI, think less like a banker and more like a partner. Address their “ask” in every sense of the word. Need help writing a letter of intent that actually gets accepted? Deal Academy has a whole course on it. To LOIs that get a second look, Sara Sharp Partner, SK&S Law Group Founder, Deal Academy P.S.
